questions.question: An application needs to store session state for a stateless web tier so that any server behind a load balancer can retrieve it with single-digit millisecond latency. Which approach is MOST appropriate?
questions.explanation: A managed in-memory cache is built for low-latency, shared session storage across multiple application servers. Object storage and relational databases have higher latency profiles for this use case, and archival storage is designed for cold data, not live session state.

questions.question: A developer is hardcoding a database password inside an application's source code. Which TWO changes should be made to follow secure secrets-management practices? (Select TWO)
options: Store the password in a managed secrets manager and retrieve it at runtime
Store the password in an environment variable encrypted with a managed encryption key
Store the password in a publicly readable storage bucket for easy access
Embed the password in the name of the resource's access role
Log the password to the application's logs for auditing
questions.explanation: A managed secrets manager and an encrypted environment variable both keep the credential out of source code while allowing secure retrieval at runtime. Public buckets, resource names, and logs are all inappropriate and insecure places to store credentials.

questions.question: A team wants to deploy a new version of an application with zero downtime and the ability to automatically roll back if error-rate alarms indicate a problem. Which deployment approach should they use?
options: An in-place deployment that stops and replaces instances one at a time
A blue/green deployment with automated rollback tied to health alarms
Manually stopping and starting instances during a maintenance window
Rebuilding the entire environment from scratch for every release
questions.explanation: A blue/green deployment shifts traffic to a new environment and can automatically roll back based on health alarms, achieving zero downtime with safe rollback. The other options either cause downtime or lack automated rollback.
